evidence.note: Best comeback arc of the batch. The player was down 15 to 116 after being pulled off the top at turn 34, then ran off Hurricanrana for 22 (37), Vertical suplex for 16 (39), Running dropkick for 19 (43), Straight right for 7 (45), Roundhouse kick for 9 (47) and Grapple counter for 5 (49) - taking Hall from 116 to 38 while never leaving 15 health themselves.

The one time in this batch a groggy setup was actually cashed: turn 38 'Hall rises - still groggy from the impact!', then the turn 39 menu offers index 1 Vertical suplex at 72% with note 'TARGET GROGGY payoff: heavy damage is available now', the player takes it, and it hits for 16. That is the setup/payoff loop working end to end.

And the counter-example one turn later. With Hall still groggy the player chose 'Hit the ropes' instead of the same 72% suplex, and Hall simply cleared it at turn 42 with 'Hall steadies themselves - they're back!' Nothing warned that walking away from a groggy opponent forfeits the window.

Real two-way threat throughout: Hall's Superplex hit for 29 twice (turns 8 and 20), taking the player from 125 to 96 and then 68 to 39. Neither wrestler was ever safe, which is why 56 turns still reads as a fight rather than a stall.

The sag is in the middle: turns 21-32 are get_up (21, 22), shake the cobwebs (23, 25), a whiffed break (27), side headlock for 6 (28), break the grapple (29), a reversal (30), recover (31) - twelve turns for 22 damage and no position progress.

Intent, label and outcome align exactly where it matters most: 'Big swing' / 'Vertical suplex' / '72%' / 'TARGET GROGGY payoff: heavy damage is available now' produced 'Hitman snaps off vertical suplex - Hall takes 16 damage.' A new player could act on that prompt correctly with no prior knowledge.

The finisher-to-cover rule is explained in-line rather than assumed. Turn 54 states the setup ('- FINISHER - the next cover packs extra heat.') and turn 56 states the cash-in with a number ('The finisher still echoes - +12 on the cover!'), so the cause of the successful pin is legible after the fact.

Recurring mislabel: when grappled the only two options are 'Grapple counter' (69%) and 'Break the grapple' (79%), both filed under intent 'Safe offense' with the note 'steady damage and momentum without overcommitting'. Turn 29's successful break logs 'Hitman: Break the grapple.' with health unchanged at 24/116 - no damage at all. The higher percentage reads like the better attack when it is not an attack.

Four single-choice turns (9, 13, 21, 55) offer only 'Fight to your feet'. At turn 55, on 1 health after the Razor's Edge, the note 'stand before they cover you; misses build escape momentum' is honest about the stakes, but the player has no decision to make in the most tense moment of the match.

Groggy-state prompts read cleanly as a modifier, not a position: state shows position STANDING with groggy true, and the failed attempt is explained plainly - 'Hitman lunges wildly but can't connect - still groggy!' with momentum dropping 3 -> 2.

stickiness.rematch_reason: This match produced the one thing the other two seeds never did: a clean, legible climax. The player survived on 15 health for eighteen turns and cut Hall down from 116 to 38, then lost to a Razor's Edge (54), a failed get-up (55) and a cover that explicitly cashed the finisher heat (56, '+12 on the cover!'). Losing that way makes me want to replay it, which is the strongest stickiness signal in the batch.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 219 taking the 72% 'TARGET GROGGY payoff' Vertical suplex at turn 41 instead of Hit the ropes, and choosing Desperation strike over Shake the cobwebs at turn 53, to test whether cashing the second groggy window closes Hall out before the Razor's Edge lands - and whether the pin at 56 can be turned into a near-fall rather than a clean three.

evidence.note: The both-on-the-top-rope Superplex for 29 damage is the biggest single hit in the batch and it fired twice (8, 20), which makes the top-rope mirror position something I want to deliberately set up rather than fall into.

The rope-running branch resolved for the first time in this batch - 'Hitman snaps off running dropkick - Hall takes 19 damage.' - out of a four-option menu (Springboard crossbody, Kill the run, Running dropkick, Spinning heel kick), leaving three named lines still unexplored.

The loss lands as earned rather than arbitrary: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge - Hitman takes 20 damage.' followed by the finisher-heat note, then the cover two turns later. Ignoring win/loss for fairness purposes, the sequencing is what creates the rematch pull.

Strongest payoff chain in the batch, and it pays off a flag set two turns earlier. The pinfall finish_sequence runs five steps - '+12 on the cover!' (0.0s), 'Referee: 1...' (1.0s), 'Referee: 2...' (1.5s), 'Referee: 3!' (0.0s), '*** PINFALL - Hall wins ***' (0.0s) - so the count is paced rather than dumped, and the +12 explicitly ties the result back to the turn 54 finisher.

Big spots hit hard and shift state visibly: 'Hall snaps off superplex - Hitman takes 29 damage.' plus 'Hitman is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.', with both wrestlers dropping to GROUNDED - a distinctive state that no other move in the match produced.

The comeback beats are individually flavoured rather than recycled: hurricanrana for 22 with a rattled callout (37), vertical suplex for 16 with another (39), running dropkick for 19 (43). log_uniqueness_ratio 0.6389 is the highest of the three seeds and it is noticeable in the read.

The failed get-up right before the cover is a genuine dread beat: 'Hitman tries to rise but can't find it - still down and vulnerable to a cover!' on 1 health, immediately followed by the pin. The state feedback does the dramatic work without extra prose.

Held back from 5 by near_fall_count 0. The referee count went straight to three on the only cover of the match, so the count sequence never delivered a kickout - the single biggest drama beat available to the format is still unfired across this entire batch.

top_issues.summary: 56 turns against a [8, 40] band. The overrun concentrates in turns 21-32, where get_up (21, 22), shake the cobwebs (23, 25), a whiffed break (27), a break (29), a reversal (30) and a recover (31) consume twelve turns for 22 total damage while both wrestlers stay STANDING or GRAPPLED.
top_issues.suggested_area: game.py turn economy for recovery-state moves (get_up, shake_groggy, break_grapple), which currently cost a full turn each and can chain

top_issues.summary: near_fall_count is 0 and only one cover was attempted in the whole match. The single pin at turn 56 went 1-2-3 clean, so the format's best drama device - the two-count kickout - never fired. Combined with seeds 226 and 210 also at zero, near-falls appear to be effectively unreachable in current tuning.
top_issues.suggested_area: pin resolution thresholds / PinSequence, so covers against a healthier opponent produce a two-count kickout instead of resolving binary

top_issues.summary: Health floors at 1, so the last two turns played out with the player already unkillable-but-beaten: turn 54's Razor's Edge took 11 health down to 1, and the only remaining question was whether the cover connected. Damage stops carrying meaning once either wrestler bottoms out.
top_issues.suggested_area: finish conditions at minimum health - consider a ref stoppage or a visible 'on the brink' state so the last turns read differently

top_issues.summary: The grappled menu presents 'Break the grapple' as intent 'Safe offense' with the note 'steady damage and momentum without overcommitting' at 79%, above 'Grapple counter' at 69% (turns 27, 29, 49). The break deals no damage - turn 29 logs only 'Hitman: Break the grapple.' - so the highest number in a two-option menu is the one that does nothing offensively.
top_issues.suggested_area: _curate_move_choices() intent assignment: break_grapple belongs under 'Reset / recover'

top_issues.summary: No loop-tax feedback fired anywhere in these 56 turns - no 'stalls out', 'getting predictable', 'telegraphed' or 'empty climb' line appears. Back-to-back climbs at turns 33 and 35, with the player getting pulled off for 6 damage in between at turn 34, drew no telegraphed-climb warning, so a punished repeat went unremarked.
top_issues.suggested_area: loop-tax thresholds for climb repetition, especially repeats that follow a failed attempt
